segments.text: Your SMT line runs fast. Then the boards wait in front of manual radial insertion: similar parts get swapped, leads are bent by hand, and quality changes from shift to shift.
segments.chapter: When manual radial insertion is the bottleneck

segments.text: The S3010A from Southern Machinery is an in-line radial insertion machine. A ten-station component sequencer and a servo-driven inserter in one frame, with automatic PCB loading and unloading.
Here is one cycle. Taped radial parts, like electrolytic capacitors, LEDs and transistors, are fed from the stations in program order.
segments.chapter: Sequencer feeds parts in program order

segments.text: Chain clips carry each part toward the insertion head, so the right part always arrives next.
The component transfer unit hands it over to the head.
The head cuts the part from its tape and forms the leads.
segments.chapter: Cut from tape and form the leads

segments.text: Meanwhile, the X Y table and turntable move the PCB under the head, and the vision system corrects the position from the fiducial marks.
The leads go straight down into the holes.
From below, the cut and clinch unit trims the leads and bends them in an N-type clinch. If a lead misses its hole, the machine stops with an alarm.
segments.chapter: N-type cut and clinch, insertion check

segments.text: The head returns, and the next part is already waiting.

Lead spans of 2.5, 5.0 and 7.5 millimetres, with 3.5 and 10 millimetre tooling also listed. Clinch length from 1.5 to 2.2 millimetres, at 10 to 35 degrees. Boards from 50 by 50 up to 400 by 400 millimetres.
segments.chapter: Lead spans, clinch and PCB size

segments.text: The specification speed is 18,000 components per hour; real output depends on your board, and we confirm it with a sample run. Programs come from Excel or CAD coordinates and are taught with the camera. And it runs in-line with loaders, unloaders and our axial and odd-form machines.
Send us your PCB file, BOM and annual volume. We run a sample with your own parts, send you the video, and quote the same day. Email info at smthelp dot com.

seo.description:
Your SMT line runs fast, then boards wait in front of manual radial insertion. The S3010A from Southern Machinery is an in-line radial insertion machine: a 10-station component sequencer and a servo-driven inserter in one frame, with automatic PCB loading and unloading.

One insertion cycle
• Taped radial parts (E-caps, LEDs, transistors) are fed from the stations in program order
• Chain clips carry each part toward the insertion head
• The CTA (component transfer unit) hands it to the head
• The head cuts the part from its tape and forms the leads
• The X/Y table and turntable position the PCB; vision corrects from the MARK points
• The leads go straight down into the holes
• The cut & clinch unit trims and N-clinches the leads from below; a missed lead stops the machine with an alarm

Key data
• Lead spans 2.5 / 5.0 / 7.5 mm (3.5 and 10.0 mm tooling listed)
• Clinch length 1.5–2.2 mm, angle 10–35°, adjustable
• PCB 50 × 50 to 400 × 400 mm, 0.79–2.36 mm thick
• Specification speed 18,000 CPH; real output depends on the board and is confirmed with a sample run
• Programs from Excel/CAD coordinates by USB, camera teaching
• In-line with loaders, unloaders, S4000 axial and S7020T terminal machines
• 220 V AC 1-phase, 0.6 MPa air; core machine 1800 × 1600 × 1800 mm, approx. 1000 kg

Insertion angle conflict (待确认): PPT/landing 0–360° in 1° steps; manual turntable rotates 90° CW/CCW. Angle not claimed in the video.
